title: Perimeter telemetry orchestrator for on-prem tenant shielding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight perimeter telemetry orchestrator that runs in customer VPCs / on-prem clusters to provide tenant-aware buffering, dynamic routing, and quarantine controls for traces, metrics, and logs. This component sits in front of existing collectors and provides a predictable, auditable boundary for multi-tenant Private/Dedicated deployments without requiring per-tenant sidecars in every pod.

Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Private often have heterogeneous agent setups and unpredictable telemetry bursts that overwhelm collector endpoints or leak cross-tenant context. Existing approaches (full sidecar per workload, heavy edge proxies) either increase operational surface area or are too coarse-grained for tenancy isolation. We need a deployable orchestrator that enforces per-tenant limits, repairs malformed trace headers, and provides safe replay and quarantine for misbehaving tenants.

Goals:
- Prevent cross-tenant contamination at the perimeter and guarantee trace/metric separation semantics.
- Provide graceful backpressure and tenant-level buffering with configurable SLOs (ingest latency < 30s for buffered items under normal load).
- Offer an operator-friendly control-plane for pinning tenant policies, quarantine ejections, and retention overrides.
- Integrate with Console dashboards and create latency/error dashboards per tenant and per collector.
- Minimal changes to customer agents: orchestrator adapts to common agent protocols (OTLP/grpc, protobuf/HTTP, syslog).

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for long-term storage solutions (still forward to central telemetry pipelines).
- Not responsible for schema translation beyond header normalization and light envelope validation.

Design overview:
- Lightweight daemonset + control-plane CRDs for on-prem; managed VM appliance for VPCs where daemonset not acceptable.
- Ingest layer accepts OTLP/gRPC and HTTP protobuf/JSON.
- Tenant identification via: explicit tenant header (x-rw-tenant), token introspection (short path to control-plane), and fallback to cluster tenant mapping.
- Per-tenant policy store synced from control-plane: rate limits, max-buffer-size, quarantinable (boolean), sampling overrides, retention hints.
- Buffering engine: per-tenant ring buffers with E2E checksums, watermarking, and optional local persistence (encrypted WAL) to survive restarts.
- Quarantine flow: on policy breach or schema failure, events are marked quarantined and routed to a tenant-specific quarantine queue/namespace; operators are alerted in Console and can inspect/approve replays.
- Trace hook repairs: normalize trace IDs, enforce parent-child invariants, and drop cross-tenant parent links with audit entries.
- Telemetry metadata emitted for Console: ingress_latency_ms, per_tenant_ingest_rate, buffer_fill_pct, quarantine_rate, malformed_event_rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deployed daemonset in staging cluster with feature-flags for OTLP and HTTP ingestion.
- Per-tenant buffer isolation: induce 5x normal burst for tenant A while other tenants maintain <2% latency increase.
- Quarantine and replay path validated end-to-end (UI action triggers replay to central pipeline).
- Console dashboards render per-tenant latency and quarantine counts; retention metadata surfaced.
- Security review completed for WAL encryption and header token handling.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype buffer engine and header normalization library (2 weeks).
2) Build ingestion adapters (OTLP gRPC + HTTP) and basic policy store sync (CRD + control-plane stub) (2 weeks).
3) Integrate quarantine/replay UI hooks and Console metrics (1 week).
4) Hardening: persistence encryption, RBAC for replay, observability metrics and traces (1 week).
5) Staging rollout + chaos tests (1 week).

Rollout strategy:
- Start with internal staging and a single customer pilot under NDA.
- Default disabled for new Private installs; opt-in via config.
- Provide upgrade playbook and data-migration scripts for existing sidecar customers.

Testing and validation:
- Load tests: tenant burst scenarios with 500k trace events/minute to verify isolation and buffer behavior.
- Fault injection: kill control-plane sync to ensure graceful degraded mode (accept telemetry with cached policies).
- Security tests: WAL key rotation, token revocation, and header replay detection.

Open decisions and trade-offs:
- Persistence: in-memory-only buffers are faster but risk data loss on restart. We default to small encrypted WAL with configurable policy.
- Tenant id resolution: header-first is fast but can be spoofed; will combine with token introspection for higher-trust tenants.
- Where to surface cost/ingest alerts for customers (Console vs email vs PagerDuty) — default to Console and allow alerting integrations.

Related artifacts:
- Design sketch: https://drive.redwood.company/observability/perimeter-orchestrator/sketch-v1
- Proto definitions: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-protos/pull/93
- Control-plane CRD docs: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OBS/Perimeter+Orchestrator+CRDs

Acceptance tests (automated):
- per-tenant-buffering.spec (k6)
- quarantine-replay-flow.test (integration)
- header-repair.unit (golang)
